text: Always look for a referral path to each top-tier target employer before applying cold: referred candidates reached interviews at about 40% against 3% for inbound applicants (Ashby, selection-confounded, so treat it as an upper bound).
Always prepare a counter for every job offer, backed by a BLS OEWS figure for the metro and role: those who countered got about 12% more, and 85% of counters got something (UCLA Anderson).
Apply first to postings under about two weeks old, and mark those over 60 days as likely stale: surveys put ghost postings at roughly a fifth of listings.

Limit tailoring of each application to about 20 minutes, using the posting's own words: the evidence for tailoring is vendor data only, while a referral or outreach note on the same application moves the odds more.
Cite BLS OEWS for the metro area and occupation code (median and 25th/75th percentiles, with the survey year) for every salary claim; job-board estimates are secondary.
Record every job application with its channel (cold, referral, recruiter, outreach, event, internal); the response rate by channel decides where the next week's hours go.
